subject: Post-demo recap: procurement gate, payment routes, hosting tradeoffs

Subject: Post-demo recap: procurement gate, payment routes, hosting tradeoffs

Hi Emma and Rajesh,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — appreciate the candid questions on latency and data isolation. Quick written recap and a short set of questions to help us align with your procurement process before we loop legal/procurement.

Summary from our side:
- Demo focus: retrieval-augmented generation at 100k tokens/day, 95th pctl latency target ~250ms.
- Hosting options discussed: hosted (API), dedicated (reserved GPU pools), private (VPC/on-prem).
- Pricing reference attached: Redwood_Pricing_20261209.pdf (attachment stub).

Procurement/readiness questions:
1) Payment method preference: do you need a purchase order (PO) and net-30 invoice, or can you pay by corporate card / marketplace purchase?
2) Marketplace interest: if you prefer to buy via a cloud marketplace, is that a hard requirement or a convenience?
3) Commit comfort: for dedicated capacity, we typically require a committed monthly spend. Would your finance team consider a 6- or 12-month committed contract, or is on-demand required?
4) SOW and procurement paperwork: do you want a short SOW + standard terms, or will your legal want to redline an enterprise agreement?

Proposed next steps:
- If PO is needed, we can prepare an invoice path and sample SOW.
- If marketplace is required, we can surface available SKUs and expected lead times.
- If you want a short procurement sync, propose a 30 min call with your procurement + legal and our AE + solutions engineer.

Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_20261209.pdf (pricing summary, hosting comparisons, commit vs on-demand examples)

Look forward to your notes — I can coordinate the procurement sync if you confirm attendees and preferred times.

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement gate, payment routes, hosting tradeoffs

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. Quick answers from procurement side:
- Payment: our preferred route is PO with net-30. We can do marketplace purchases but procurement will only allow that for smaller pilots under our card program. For production capacity, we will need invoiced PO terms.
- Marketplace: convenient for early proof-of-concept, but not a blocker. Production procurement prefers direct invoicing.
- Commits: we are open to a 6 month minimum for dedicated if the pricing supports predictable unit costs; legal will want to review term lengths.
- SOW: please send a short SOW and your standard enterprise terms. Legal will route any redlines back to you; timeline depends on the size of the commitment.

I will loop in our procurement lead (Rajesh cc'd) when we set the sync. Proposed timeline: procurement review next week is realistic.

Best,
Emma Thompson
Head of Platform Engineering | Orion AI
emma@orionai.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement gate, payment routes, hosting tradeoffs

Hi Emma, Rajesh — thanks for the fast reply. Adding a few operational clarifications so procurement has the exact options when you discuss internally.

1) Billing flows we can support:
- PO / invoice (net 30 or net 45) billed monthly for hosted API and embeddings; invoice route works for reserved capacity (Dedicated) as well but requires a contract and billing contact.
- Marketplace purchase: immediate payment via card through the cloud vendor; good for pilots and smaller usage, not ideal for enterprise invoicing.

2) Hosting tradeoffs (short):
- Hosted (API): fastest onboarding, no infra work, monthly usage invoice, good for pilots and production with standard RBAC and audit logs.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable per-token unit economics, requires a commit (6 or 12 months typical) and ~2-4 week provisioning lead time. Invoicing handled under the reserved capacity contract.
- Private: full VPC or on-prem; requires security review and an enterprise onboarding project, longer lead time and separate licensing.

3) Paperwork and SOW: attached SOW-draft.docx (stub). This is a short technical SOW we use for dedicated pilots; includes success criteria, SLAs, and onboarding milestones. Also linking our procurement playbook for reference: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSOWtemplate

If Orion confirms PO + net-30 for production, we will pull in our finance operations to prepare an invoice flow and standard billing contact form. If you prefer marketplace for the pilot, we can provide a SKU list and expected costs per region.

Proposed action before the sync:
- Rajesh, can you confirm preferred PO terms (net 30/45) and whether procurement needs our W-9 or local tax docs?
- Emma, can you confirm whether the initial pilot will be hosted or dedicated? If hosted, we can provision tomorrow. If dedicated, we will need to confirm commit level.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
